text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed ~3% of invoice preview diffs this morning tied to 'late aggregate' records hitting the billing window after preview generation. Looks like compact-agg windowing + our enrich backfill race.
jon: ugh. Is that the same late-arrival we saw last month?
maya: same pattern but different cause. last month was proxy reorder; this time the aggregator commit lagged behind enrich consumer, so credits got applied after preview snapshot.
liam: do we have a query to surface affected tenants? quick grep could help.
maya: yeah, running a quick one: ```sql
SELECT tenant_id, count(*) AS late_events
FROM billing.events
WHERE event_time BETWEEN '2025-03-16T09:00:00Z' AND '2025-03-16T10:00:00Z'
AND processed_at > snapshot_time
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY late_events DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
rebecca: can we detect this at preview time and flag the invoice as "potentially incomplete" in the console instead of surprising customers?
sarah: short-term we can add a subtle banner on invoice-preview: "Preview may exclude late-arriving usage" with a link to docs. Long-term we should tie preview generation to a watermark on the aggregate stream.
jon: watermarks are the right call, but they add latency to previews. Product will push back if previews slow. Maybe show a watermark age metric instead?
liam: alternative: expose a per-tenant late_event_rate in the console and attach a risk score. No preview delay, but visibility.
maya: agreed — risk score + banner is lowest-friction. Also ops: can we backfill for impacted tenants now?
ops-bot: @maya backfill job queued: billing-backfill-20250316-09 (ETA 18m). Will post status updates.
rebecca: UX note — show when preview was generated and the stream watermark it used. That keeps us honest.
jon: there's also an internal API debate: do we make the dedupe/fuzzy-window config editable per-tenant (customer teams asked) or keep it global? If we make it per-tenant, previews become harder to reason about.
sarah: per-tenant configs -> huge support surface. Start with per-product-tier toggles (free/pro/enterprise).
liam: ops question: if we start surfacing risk scores, do downstream billing pipelines need schema changes? I want to avoid churn.
maya: risk_score can be computed on the UI side from existing telemetry (late_events / total_events). No pipeline schema change required.
jon: sweet. For the backfill, make sure we dedupe against previously applied credits. Last time we double-applied and had to rollback.
liam: put an idempotency check in the backfill: ```python
if ledger.has_credit(event.id): continue
apply_credit(event)
```
ops-bot: backfill job started. 0/12 shards complete. Progress updates: 25% at 10m, 50% at 12m.
billing-bot: alert: invoice-preview delta > $5000 for 4 tenants due to late aggregates (auto-created tickets: BILL-1021..BILL-1024).
rebecca: let's triage the enterprise tenants first and send a polite heads-up email template. I'll draft one.
sarah: follow-ups: (1) add preview banner + watermark age metric (2) compute per-tenant late_event_rate for console (3) implement idempotent backfill then audit ledger (4) document dedupe/window semantics for support.
maya: I'll own the audit and the console banner PR. Jon/Liam can you pair on the backfill idempotency change?
jon: yes. I'll sync with Liam after standup.
liam: ack.
maya: thanks. tagging this thread for postmortem notes.
ops-bot: backfill job complete: success. 12/12 shards. Applied 1,342 credits, skipped 98 duplicates. Summary: https://console.internal/billing/backfill/1737654321
rebecca: great — I'll send the tenant emails and update the incident notes.
jon: follow-up todo: add a small telemetry counter for "events_after_snapshot" emitted by the aggregator so we can alert before preview runs.
sarah: can we have a lightweight alert: if events_after_snapshot / window_size > 0.005 for > 10m then page oncall?
liam: yes, we can add that as a KQL rule. I'll file a ticket.
maya: closing loop — we should schedule a short retro on whether previews should use stricter watermarks or UI signals. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
